summary.name: Practical Linux Infrastructure
summary.one_liner: A 2014 Apress book by Syed Ali that teaches how to build or modify a Linux infrastructure using open source tools such as KVM, Puppet, HAProxy, Nagios and BIND.
keywords: linux troubleshooting top netstat iostat vmstat
use_cases: Building a new enterprise-grade Linux infrastructure
Configuring load balancing and high availability
Monitoring servers with Nagios and Cacti
Troubleshooting CPU, memory, disk and network issues on Linux servers
summary.what_it_does: This is a book (Apress, eBook published 29 December 2014, 320 pages) that walks through building or altering a Linux infrastructure with open source tools. It covers virtualization with KVM, hosting on Google Cloud Platform, and configuration management with Puppet. It also covers version control with Git, email with Postfix, databases with MySQL, and web serving with Apache. High availability is covered with HAProxy and Keepalived, monitoring with Cacti and Nagios, and DNS with BIND. The book also covers DHCP, VPN and iptables remote access, and troubleshooting tools such as top, netstat, iostat and vmstat.
notable: Covers a broad stack of open source tools for building Linux infrastructure
Step-by-step instructions and examples in each of 10 chapters
Written by a senior site reliability engineering manager
caveats: Paid book; the page shows purchase/access options with tax calculated at checkout
Published in 2014, so tool versions and cloud details may be dated
Accessibility information is marked as coming soon
